_comment: The worked example: this repository's own code-index config, shipped so the ~10% that
binds a generator like this to a codebase's house conventions is visible rather than
described. Every field below encodes a convention THIS repo happens to follow; a repo
that writes its headers, flags or emphasis differently changes them here and changes
Honest note: the original repo this skill was first built in is not public, so the
worked example is this one. It exercises every field.
_header: House convention: `// name.mjs — what it is`, on one of the first few lines. The em
dash matters. A plain hyphen appears in ordinary prose, and matching it would claim the
first commented line of any file as its description.
_cli: A file has a command surface only if it reads process.argv. Without that condition,
every library mentioning a flag inside a help string acquires an imaginary CLI.
_why: Emphasis convention: this codebase SHOUTS its load-bearing invariants inside comments
('NO TOOL-RESULT CONTENT ... IS EVER PRINTED'). Three or more consecutive capitalised
words in a comment is the signal. Capped at 2 per file — WHY is a pointer to the thing
worth reading, not a second copy of it.
_guard: Where the checks live. Test files are deliberately included: they are the group that
breaks first when an export changes, and the first version of this excluded them and
so reported the most reliable early warning in the repo as absent.
_manifestThreshold: A file naming more than this share of the ELIGIBLE files is a register, not a caller.
The denominator is the eligible set — the files this index covers — never the whole
tree. Against the whole tree, padding a repo with docs makes a register look like a
minority and it slips back through as a caller of everything.
